summary: cinepi-raw (63a08d5) writes CinemaDNG with a 3-stage chain: main loop queues a POINTER into the libcamera buffer (no copy on the completion or main thread); N encode workers (Cinemate: 4, pinned to CPUs 1-2) do the single pass that reads the camera buffer row by row into a 4096-aligned, 1 MiB-rounded pooled RAM buffer (16-bit = one memcpy; 12-bit = pack; COMP1 = LUT decode + pack; log = up to 4 row passes), then release the camera buffer BEFORE any disk I/O; M disk workers (Cinemate: 2 on exFAT/NTFS, 8 on ext4) do open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC), one POSIX_FADV_SEQUENTIAL, ONE write() of the exact DNG size, close(). No fsync, no sync_file_range, no DONTNEED (removed 2026-03-06 in b71ec67), no flush at record stop. Back-pressure is a RAM permit of 0.90 x MemAvailable (measured 173 x 17 MiB = 2941 MiB on a 4 GB CM5 = 6.9 s at 25 fps 16-bit); encode workers BLOCK on it, holding camera buffers, until the camera starves; the main loop ends the take at cap-2 ("RAM pool exhausted"); Cinemate auto-stops at 90 % fill. A "drop" (droppedFrames) is ONLY a sensor-timestamp capture gap >= 2 periods counted on the encode worker; writeFailures counts open/short-write/close errors; pool exhaustion, alloc failure and dng_save throws are not counted as drops. File layout: 8-byte header, raw strip at offset 8, IFD0 (holds the raw; no SubIFD), optional thumbnail strip + IFD1 (Cinemate default: colour JPEG 640x360, ~16 KB, +4.0 ms/frame). Camera buffers: --buffer-count 10 on exFAT/NTFS, 8 on ext4/default, 6 bare. Whole process is launched under chrt -f 70 / ionice -c2 -n0 / taskset -c 1-3; the --disk-nice -5 fails with EPERM on the rig. Fairness: cinepi-raw DID drop frames at 4K 16-bit ClearHDR in Sept 2026 (208 events 2026-09-15; earlier 102 in 20 min) from the ccmpPreview post-process stage, fixed 2026-09-15 for 16-bit (12-bit still re-renders at ~35 ms/frame); there is no long exFAT 4K25 16-bit measurement in the handbook, only an NTFS soak that filled the pool in 15-22 s. Full report with every ref at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/80b31005-3a15-5c7a-9048-3096078b0f85/scratchpad/research/R1.md.

findings.claim: Encode workers default 2 (Cinemate passes 4), disk workers default 8 (Cinemate 2 on exFAT/NTFS/default, 8 on ext4); workers are process-lifetime threads named dng-enc-N / dng-dsk-N; affinity rule: if the safe CPU set has >= worker count each worker gets one CPU (i % n), else all share the whole set; the last online core (audio, SCHED_FIFO 80) is stripped from any requested set.
findings.notes: On a 4-core Pi 5 with the exfat profile: 4 encode workers share {1,2}; 2 disk workers both on CPU 2; CPUs 0 and 3 never carry DNG workers.

findings.claim: Nice values do not apply on the rig: dng-dsk-N logs 'failed to set nice level -5: Permission denied' every take (service runs as pi, no RLIMIT_NICE/CAP_SYS_NICE); the encode workers' -10 fails the same way (same setpriority call).
findings.notes: Disk-worker EPERM is confirmed by the handbook log; encode-worker EPERM is inferred (same syscall, same user).

findings.claim: Cinemate wraps the whole cinepi-raw process in `chrt -f 70` (if permitted), `ionice -c2 -n0`, `taskset -c 1-3`; when chrt succeeds every thread (main, libcamera, encode, disk) is SCHED_FIFO 70 and nice is moot.
findings.notes: Unconfirmed whether chrt succeeded on the rig: look for 'RT scheduling not permitted' in the cinemate log.

findings.claim: max_ram_buffers_ = max(1, 0.90 x MemAvailable / buffer_size), read from /proc/meminfo inside setup_encoder(), which re-runs at the first frame of every take; encode workers block without timeout on the permit; disk workers release it after close(); buffer_full() = ram_buffers_ + 2 >= max; the main loop stops recording ('RAM pool exhausted') when buffer_full() and the take is not just starting.
findings.notes: buffer_size = align_up(frame + 64 KiB + log LUT + thumbnail reservation, 1 MiB) at dng_encoder.cpp:1035-1039. Pool buffers are allocated lazily with posix_memalign(4096) and recycled via buffer_pool_.

findings.claim: On the 4 GB CM5 the pool was 173 frames x 17 MiB = 2941 MiB (MemAvailable ~3.27 GiB), i.e. 6.9 s at 25 fps 16-bit; on 8 GB no measurement exists (computed ~390 frames if MemAvailable ~7.2 GiB).
findings.notes: The 8 GB figure is unconfirmed: read the 'RAM pool: up to {} frames' log line once on that board.

findings.claim: The camera buffer is HELD during the encode (from EncodeBuffer on the main thread until the encode worker finishes dng_save) and NOT during the disk write; EncodeBuffer2 queues only a pointer; the CompletedRequestPtr deleter is queueRequest, and encodeBufferDone pops the FIFO front after dng_save, returning the buffer to libcamera.
findings.notes: DMA sync: START|READ at completion (rpicam_app.cpp:1225), START|RW + END|RW both on the main thread inside EncodeBuffer (buffer_sync.cpp:16-47), END|READ at requeue (rpicam_app.cpp:1008). encode_queue_ is unbounded; the only cap on held camera buffers is libcamera running out of them.

findings.claim: Requests in flight = --buffer-count: 10 on Cinemate's exfat/ntfs profiles, 8 on ext4/default, 6 for bare cinepi-raw; the raw stream copies stream 0's count; buffers are app-allocated from /dev/dma_heap/vidbuf_cached (cached system heap on Pi 5).
findings.notes: settings.jsonc sensors.raw_buffer_count can override; the value actually used on the Pi is in the 'Camera raw-buffer headroom: --buffer-count' log line.

findings.claim: encodeBufferDone pops the FIFO front regardless of which of the 4 encode workers finished, so a camera buffer can be requeued while another worker still reads it (tearing hazard, not a drop mechanism).
findings.notes: Source-only inference; window bounded by libcamera's queued-request depth (<= buffer_count-1 frame periods).

findings.claim: 16-bit unpacked path: ONE user-space pass (per-row memcpy via write_pod into the pooled buffer) + one kernel copy in write(); 12-in-16 SDR: pack_row_16_to_12bit into a row scratch then memcpy; COMP1: LUT decode per 8-px block + pack; CineMate Log: normalise (unpack/shift), encode_row LUT in place, pack, memcpy = up to 4 row passes. All on the encode worker; none on the completion or main thread.
findings.notes: The first frame of each take also samples every 3rd row for the ClearHDR clamp detector inside the same loops (kRowStride = 3 at :1167).

findings.claim: Disk worker: open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0644), posix_fadvise(SEQUENTIAL) (the only fadvise in the file), ONE write() of buf.usedSize from a 4096-aligned buffer (no retry on short write), close() = 4 syscalls, plus one formatted 'DNG written:' stdout line per frame before the open. No fsync/fdatasync/sync_file_range/O_DIRECT/fallocate/DONTNEED anywhere; nothing at record stop.
findings.notes: Grep of dng_encoder.cpp for fsync|fdatasync|sync_file_range|O_DIRECT|O_SYNC|fallocate|ftruncate|FADV_DONTNEED|FADV_NOREUSE: only the comment at :2351 and the SEQUENTIAL hint at :2356.

findings.claim: 8-byte TIFF header; raw strip at offset 8 (StripOffsets=8, StripByteCounts=rawSize, Compression 1 only); IFD0 follows the raw data and holds it (no SubIFD); optional thumbnail strip then IFD1 chained from IFD0. Under Cinemate the thumbnail is ON by default: colour JPEG q85 at lores>>1 (640x360), reservation 691,200 B, actual ~16 KB, measured +4.0 ms/frame (+18 %) encode time.
findings.notes: cinepi-raw's own RawOptions default is thumbnail 0; the 3/1 defaults come from the controller (CP_DEF_THUMBNAIL 3, CP_DEF_THUMBNAIL_SIZE 1) and Cinemate. Snapshotted per take in setup_encoder (:1006-1007).

findings.claim: droppedFrames counts ONLY capture gaps: on the encode worker, under encode_mutex_, the sensor-timestamp delta between consecutive encoded frames rounded to >= 2 frame periods adds raw_elapsed-1. writeFailures counts open/short-write/close errors. Pool exhaustion ends the take and is not counted; posix_memalign failure and dng_save throws drop a frame with NO counter. There is no 'disk slow' counter or per-frame deadline.
findings.notes: Published per frame on the cp_stats channel: droppedFrames, writeFailures, bufferSize, bufferSizeMax (peak disk_buffer_ depth), framesInFlight (encode_queue_ + mid-encode + disk_buffer_, not reset per take).

findings.claim: COMP1 decode and 10/12-bit packing run inside dng_save on the encode worker; decoder uses 4 static 1024-entry dequant LUTs and 8-byte blocks -> 8 px, adapted from Apertar-Core's CdngEncoder; the depth rule (dng_output_depth.hpp) packs 12-in-16 SDR to 12, native 10 (incl. COMP1, rounded) to 10, keeps genuine 16-bit verbatim. Per-frame cost of COMP1->12 at 4K is not measured anywhere.
findings.notes: The cost is unconfirmed: needs a take at redis log_level debug to see 'Time taken for the encode: {} ms' (dng_encoder.cpp:2300-2301); Cinemate never sets that key. Whether Cinemate launches the imx585 4K 12-bit mode as P (COMP1) or U was not checked.

findings.claim: CineMate Log is resolved once per take in setup_encoder (source depth = sensor mode snapshot, target 10/12, refuses to linear on spec/depth/black-level mismatch; 12-bit ClearHDR only composed with the CCMP decompand to target 10) and applied per row on the encode worker as one forward-LUT lookup per sample before packing; a code comment says the LUT pass dominates dng_save on a log take.
findings.notes: Output sizes from commit 04b7332: 16->10 log 10.51 MB vs 16.81 MB linear 16-bit at 4K.

findings.claim: Record start resets per-take counters and forces setup_encoder; nothing is flushed or dropped (the previous take drains to its own folder; Cinemate blocks the rec trigger and mode-change relaunch while is_writing_buf). Record stop does nothing but close the folder and stop audio: no drain, no flush, no fsync; drain time = backlog x per-file write time, unbounded. When the disk is slower than capture: disk_buffer_ grows into the RAM pool (~7 s on 4 GB), Cinemate auto-stops at 90 % fill (4 Hz poll), otherwise encode workers block holding camera buffers, libcamera runs out of its 10 buffers, frames stop arriving (droppedFrames), main loop stops at cap-2.
findings.notes: Hardware evidence: 16-bit soaks on NTFS (fuseblk) at ~355 MB/s stalled after 15-22 s when the 173-frame pool filled, 'frames stop arriving — cleanly'. No equivalent exFAT soak exists in the handbook.

findings.claim: POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED ('drop file pages ASAP') and malloc_trim(0) were added per frame in 0981681 (2025-06-23) and removed, with NOREUSE and a per-frame info line, in b71ec67 (2026-03-06, 'streamline disk worker overhead'); the commit message gives no reason for dropping DONTNEED beyond overhead; since then the kernel's own writeback is the only flusher.
findings.notes: The RAM permit itself dates from cdbb2fb (2025-06-12 'fix frame buffering'); the buffer pool from 8fe39cc (2025-10-17); worker tuning options from d71027b (2025-09-28).

findings.claim: cinepi-raw DID drop frames at 4K 16-bit ClearHDR in September 2026 (208 drop events on 2026-09-15; an earlier '102 drops in 20 minutes' report), caused by the ccmpPreview post-process stage re-rendering the lores frame on a detached per-frame thread (measured 35 ms/frame 12-bit 4K, 22 ms 16-bit 4K); fixed for 16-bit by ea53b2c/dca6748 (operator-confirmed 2026-09-15); 12-bit ClearHDR still renders twice.
findings.notes: The operator's belief that cinemate did not drop at 4K25 16-bit is therefore true only after 2026-09-15 and only for linear 16-bit; the handbook has no 10-minute exFAT 4K25 16-bit cinepi-raw measurement at all.

findings.claim: kb a1/b1 claims re-opened in source all hold (open flags, permit formula, counters, Cinemate profiles, release-before-write, hazard); two handbook statements are wrong/stale: architecture/cinepi-raw.md says one atomic counter feeds both the RAM guard and the write indicator (the guard reads ram_buffers_ permits, not frames_in_flight_), and its output-depth section still says 10-bit is excluded from COMP1 (96f7a2a admitted it).

leads.lead: Back-pressure location: cinepi-raw blocks encode workers on a RAM permit (0.9 x MemAvailable, ~173 frames / 6.9 s on 4 GB) and never drops at the writer; Apertar's 12-frame queue drops after ~0.5 s (drop[queue-full]).
leads.mechanism: A multi-second exFAT stall (cluster allocation, trim debt, writeback burst) is absorbed in RAM in cinepi-raw and only becomes a camera starve after the pool is gone; in Apertar the same stall exceeds 12 frames and drops.
leads.evidence: dng_encoder.cpp:1079-1082, 2172-2176@63a08d5; hardware-log.md:963-967 (NTFS soak absorbed 15-22 s cleanly). The kb drop-frames README says Core now has a buffer=ram mode (0.6 x MemAvailable - 512 MiB) — not verified in Core source by this worker.
leads.how_to_test: Same exFAT drive, 4K25 16-bit, 10 min: Core buffer=frames vs buffer=ram; compare drop[queue-full], peak_queue and capture-gap. Confirm buffer=ram was actually active in the failing takes.

leads.lead: Nothing heavy runs on libcamera's completion thread in cinepi-raw; the camera buffer is read on 4 encode workers (CPUs 1-2) and returned right after the pack, before any disk I/O. Apertar (per kb) copies on the completion thread and drops at copy-slot when the copy worker holds buffers-2 requests.
leads.mechanism: Writeback bursts and exFAT allocation stalls hit whichever thread touches dirty page cache or faults memory; cinepi-raw keeps that off the thread that must requeue requests, so a kernel stall costs RAM, not frames.
leads.evidence: rpicam_app.cpp:1212-1255, post_processor.cpp:136, cinepi_recorder.hpp:49-105, dng_encoder.cpp:2239-2304@63a08d5; Apertar A2 lost 10 % at capture with no per-frame sync (kb digest).
leads.how_to_test: perf sched / trace-cmd on Apertar's completion thread during a 4K25 take with and without APERTAR_DNG_WRITEBACK; look for the copy thread blocked in page-fault or writeback paths.

leads.lead: Camera buffer headroom: cinepi-raw runs 10 raw buffers on exFAT (8 ext4, 6 bare) = 400 ms at 25 fps / 200 ms at 50 fps; Apertar runs 4 SDR / 8 ClearHDR (+2 only FAT/NTFS, 0 exFAT per kb) = 80 ms at 4K50 12-bit.
leads.mechanism: Any pipeline-thread or copy stall longer than (buffers-2) frame periods starves the CFE; at 50 fps SDR Apertar has 2 spare frames.
leads.evidence: storage_profiles.py:82,93@4990afc; rpicam_app.cpp:630-632,657@63a08d5; kb drop-frames README line 178.
leads.how_to_test: APERTAR_RAW_CAMERA_BUFFERS=10 at 4K50 12-bit on exFAT; count capture-gap and copy-slot vs the default.

leads.lead: cinepi-raw does NO sync during the take (no sync_file_range, no 1 s fsync, no DONTNEED since b71ec67) yet is believed clean; Apertar's A2 (no per-frame sync_file_range) lost 10 % at capture — so the hint is not the lever by itself; the kernel writeback knobs Cinemate sets at mount (vm.dirty_*, nr_requests) or the structural differences above must explain A2.
leads.mechanism: Without a per-frame hint the kernel flushes in dirty_expire/dirty_ratio bursts; whether that burst stalls capture depends on what runs on the completion thread and on dirty_bytes limits.
leads.evidence: dng_encoder.cpp:2351-2379@63a08d5; git show b71ec67; kb digest A2 result.
leads.how_to_test: Repeat Apertar A2 with cinemate's mount-time sysctl values applied to the same drive; if clean, the knobs are the lever and APERTAR_DNG_WRITEBACK can default off.

leads.lead: One write() per frame of the whole 16.6 MB DNG from a 4 KiB-aligned buffer (4 syscalls/frame) vs Apertar's ~40 syscalls/frame (491,520-byte chunks per kb).
leads.mechanism: Fewer syscalls and one contiguous extent request per file; on exFAT with 128 KB clusters each small write may re-enter exfat_get_block/alloc_cluster.
leads.how_to_test: strace -c -f both recorders for 60 s at 4K25; compare write() counts and time; then try a single writev/one write per frame in Core behind a knob.

leads.lead: The operator's belief 'cinemate did not drop at 4K25 16-bit on this rig' is only partly supported: cinepi-raw dropped frames at 4K 16-bit ClearHDR until 2026-09-15 (208 events; earlier 102 in 20 min) because of the ccmpPreview stage, and the handbook holds no long exFAT 4K25 16-bit cinepi-raw take at all (the only soak is NTFS and it filled the pool in 15-22 s).
leads.mechanism: cinepi-raw cannot see a slow disk until the pool is gone (~7 s), so a take shorter than that shows zero droppedFrames regardless of disk speed; a 10-minute take is needed for a like-for-like comparison.
leads.evidence: ccmpPreviewStage.cpp:178-182@63a08d5; hardware-log.md:3184-3203, 963-967, 2372; cinepi_controller.cpp:35-39@63a08d5 (zero drops benchmark was 4K 16-bit Log 12 = 12.4 MB/frame).
leads.how_to_test: Record a 10-minute 4K25 16-bit linear take with cinepi-raw on the same exFAT NVMe and read droppedFrames, writeFailures, bufferSizeMax and the 'RAM pool' line.

leads.lead: Pre-roll effect, cinepi-raw side: a 2 s take at max fps runs setup_encoder and leaves its pooled 17 MiB buffers pre-faulted in buffer_pool_ for the real take if buffer_size is unchanged (same mode/bits; fps does not change it), and warms the exFAT allocation bitmap/FAT pages for the folder. Effect on the next take's drops is unmeasured.
leads.mechanism: First-touch page faults of fresh posix_memalign buffers (4352 pages each) and cold exFAT metadata are paid during the pre-roll instead of the first second of the take.
leads.evidence: dng_encoder.cpp:2178-2184, 2407-2488@63a08d5; kb digest (pre-roll effect never measured).
leads.how_to_test: A/B 10 short takes each with pre-roll on/off in Apertar; count drops in the first 2 s; also check whether Apertar's pre-roll leaves any buffers warm (its own pool semantics).

leads.lead: Things cinepi-raw does worse that Apertar should not copy: no flush/fsync at stop (pulled drive loses up to dirty_expire and leaves 0-byte exFAT entries); no counter for alloc-fail/dng_save-throw drops; synchronous Redis pipeline and a stdout log line per frame on the capture path; a detached pthread per frame; FIFO-front camera-buffer release with 4 workers (tearing hazard); nice EPERM and probably SCHED_FIFO 70 for disk workers.
leads.mechanism: Each is a latency or integrity cost that Apertar's design already avoids or counts.
leads.evidence: cinepi_raw.cpp:431-434; dng_encoder.cpp:2186-2196, 2252-2276; cinepi_controller.cpp:686-699; post_processor.cpp:136; cinepi_recorder.hpp:158-174@63a08d5; open-threads.md:340-356; cinepi_multi.py:276-288@4990afc.
leads.how_to_test: Not needed for the drop question; listed so the comparison is fair.
